expected_before_changes.reason: Provisional keywords + reports BR002295, BR004918, BR004979; mixed/generic cues retained as unclear; human review pending.
Provisional keywords + reports BR002387, BR002467, BR002668; mixed/generic cues retained as unclear; human review pending.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Collision and traffic-enforcement reports share a broad traffic theme.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR003469 and BR004767 describe collisions; random BR001395 concerns impaired/unlicensed driving. The broad traffic definition covers these, but the topic is not a collision-only category.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Theft and burglary are merged by apprehension wording.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004812 includes pickpocketing and shoplifting; BR001684 and random BR000599 describe break-ins. Neither Theft nor Burglary fits the entire cluster.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Multiple victims/episodes and overlapping weapons cues.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR003466, BR004331 and random BR000283 all describe attacks or knife injuries. Assault/threats is supported in these examples; weapon mentions do not make the primary incident a weapons-only report.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Theft, robbery and multi-incident arrest summaries coexist.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002259 combines distraction theft and street robberies; BR003559 involves a struggle over property; random BR002374 is an armed pharmacy robbery. A single primary offense is not defensible cluster-wide.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Political wording can coexist with property damage.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR001514, BR003163 and random BR000319 describe graffiti or painted facades. Damage is explicit; political slogans alone do not establish a hate motivation.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Joint inspections also discuss gambling, weapons and hygiene.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR001069 and BR001235 lead with anti-drug operations but cover other violations; random BR001574 describes a cocaine seizure. Retain the drug theme provisionally and review multi-offense reports individually.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Attempted robbery must remain included; suspect descriptions are incidental.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004307, BR002399 and random BR003657 describe demands for money using firearms, knives or blows. The last attempt failed but still fits the robbery/attempt definition.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Fire reports are not automatically proven arson.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR005087, BR003845 and random BR001704 concern vehicle fires or an arson investigation/update. The descriptive fire category fits without asserting confirmed criminal intent for every report.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Assembly reports can contain separate graffiti or regulatory offenses.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004321 mixes assembly reporting with other incidents; BR004326 is a deployment notice; random BR001329 describes a peaceful rally. Retain event information provisionally, but review substantive incident-led exceptions.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Prevention text mentions crimes without reporting a new victim incident.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004058 announces school-route banners, BR000983 gives festival safety information, and random BR003488 describes bicycle registration. These are public-information/prevention reports, not theft incident counts.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Deception and theft overlap at the doorstep.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002877, BR002081 and random BR003724 describe impersonated utility workers obtaining entry and stealing. The existing fraud/deception codebook explicitly includes fake workers; report-level theft overlap should remain documented.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Generic witness appeals and suspect details accompany actual violence.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004417, BR000749 and random BR001481 describe physical attacks and injuries. The assault/threats proposal follows the incident, not the appeal wording.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Theft of jewelry is downstream of unlawful entry.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR005000, BR002845 and random BR001809 describe entering houses or a mosque by breaking/opening entry points and taking property. Burglary is supported by the entry context.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Jewelry/watch wording groups robbery with nonviolent taking and display damage.
assessments.evidence_explanation: The first three examples show force or injury, but counterexamples BR000317 and BR001250 concern distraction taking and a smashed shop display. Keep unclear; do not infer robbery from a watch/chain keyword.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Many counts are violations inside one police report.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004431, BR004300 and random BR002389 concern speed/vehicle enforcement. Retain the broad traffic category; do not treat the number of violations as the report count.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Football boilerplate includes prevention warnings rather than new crimes.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002898, BR003042 and random BR000460 describe match logistics, road closures and preventive advice. Public information is better supported than a traffic-incident or burglary assignment.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Warnings summarize multiple actual or attempted fraud cases.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002228 and BR002908 describe deceptive investment platforms; random BR003654 describes impersonation/shock calls and loss. The fraud theme is supported, without equating each report with a single victim or completed offense.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: The weapons label hides attacks explicitly excluded by its codebook rule.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002295 and BR004918 concern weapons/replicas, but random BR000915 describes shooting irritant gas at neighbors and dangerous assault. The existing Weapons-related definition excludes confirmed attacks as primary; keep the mixed cluster unclear.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Handbag/senior wording mixes robbery, theft warnings and burglary-related violence.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR001300 and BR001971 describe force or injury; random BR001315 combines impersonation/confinement and knife robbery. Counterexamples BR003296 and BR003278 add nonviolent bicycle-basket theft/prevention and a break-in with assault. No cluster-wide Theft or Robbery label.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: War-ordnance disposal is not evidence of a contemporary crime.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR001474, BR000303 and random BR001278 describe evacuation and disposal of suspected war bombs. The existing descriptive ordnance category fits; do not call all such reports arson or explosive offenses.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Shipping locations do not define the offense; some incidents occur outside Bremen city.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR001475, BR001380 and random BR001787 describe ballast-water or water-pollution violations. Retain environmental/regulatory provisionally; retain original geography and avoid geographic crime-rate claims.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Event-based clustering hides multiple substantive offense types.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002387 contains robbery, assault and pyrotechnics; BR002467 includes injuries, explosives and theft; random BR002622 concerns traffic offenses and weapons during election celebrations. This exceeds prevention/logistics, so the public-information label is misleading.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: General police warnings and other seized objects are secondary.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR003370 and BR001880 concern hate postings/prohibited symbols; random BR004028 describes a prohibited salute. Hate/discrimination is supported as a reporting theme, not a legal finding of guilt.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Explosion, damage and theft can appear in the same report.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002955, BR004761 and random BR002184 describe vending-machine detonations. The existing explosion category fits the incident mechanism; theft/damage overlap requires a consistent primary-category rule.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Corona/nightlife boilerplate merges notices, violence, drugs and road enforcement.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004204 and BR004257 summarize heterogeneous operations; random BR004243 announces curfew rules. The shared setting/regulation wording is not a coherent incident category.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: A response/disposition cluster is not a crime or medical diagnosis category.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR001202 concerns threats, BR001269 includes knife violence, and random BR003369 concerns a fire and resistance. Psychiatric-response wording does not justify assigning one crime type.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Road/goods checks are mixed with animal welfare and animal rescue reports.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR003183, BR002673 and random BR003153 concern vehicle/goods inspections, but counterexamples BR000336 and BR000541 describe abandoned cats and a killed swan. Neither Traffic-related nor Environmental/regulatory covers all without a new team rule.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Suspicious-mail wording is not proof of an explosion or hazardous substance.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004313 and random BR003812 explicitly report harmless substances; BR005105 combines powder letters and knives on playgrounds. Do not force a fire/explosion label; inspect threat/hoax incidents individually.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Violence overlaps with alleged hate motivation.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR003180 and random BR000620 describe discriminatory abuse and attacks; BR003270 contains multiple incidents with different identity/motivation evidence. Retain the hate theme provisionally, but reviewers must verify motivation report by report.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Money laundering is not automatically the same as victim-facing fraud.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR000624, BR000371 and random BR001535 describe false identities, accounts and proceeds. Ask the team whether the codebook should cover financial offenses more broadly; do not silently stretch Fraud/deception.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Missing-person notices and unconfirmed events do not establish a crime.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002174 explicitly lacks confirmation; BR004391 is a missing-person search; random BR001194 cancels a search with no criminal indications. Preserve unknown/non-crime uncertainty instead of inventing a victim/crime category.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Death investigations are not necessarily homicide.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004232, BR001814 and random BR000111 concern drowning or a body linked to a swimming disappearance. The non-traffic accident/death-inquiry category fits without assuming foul play.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: A firearm keyword must be interpreted through the injury/attack context.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR000360, BR000009 and random BR000000 describe people shot and investigations of attacks. Assault/threats is better supported than the possession/replica-weapons category.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Search-success/deletion boilerplate combines laundering and fraud updates.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR002354 and BR002215 concern laundering/false accounts; random BR002688 concerns a bank-impersonation fraud investigation. Resolve the financial-offense/codebook boundary before a cluster-level label.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Repeated head-kick warnings are boilerplate but the source incidents are assaults.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004092, BR005104 and random BR002488 all describe attacks and injury. The substantive incident supports Assault/threats; the shared warning alone would not establish it.

assessments.possible_mapping_problems: Resistance/apprehension is shared reporting language across different incidents.
assessments.evidence_explanation: BR004424 and BR001335 combine violence, damage and resistance; random BR001005 is rescue of a fleeing person with drugs found later. A single violence, drug or damage label would hide unrelated subjects.
